Why: 1 uM showed large-nucleus z=61, multinucleation z=13, contracted bright actin that I read as cytokinesis failure/antimitotic, and its atlas at 0.75 similarity tied vincristine/demecolcine 5/10 vs protein-synthesis 4/10; 10 uM had only 6 cells with saturated compact tubulin and weak 0.43-0.51 stabilizer neighbours that e4 said cannot exclude destabilizers. Combined-well atlas then flipped to protein-synthesis 5/10. With no DNA-damage/replication neighbours and no 0.3 uM well (budget spent), I over-weighted mitotic mimicry.

Literature now clarifies topo II poison identity: Evison et al Med Res Rev PMID 26286294 "More than Just Another Topoisomerase II Poison"; topo II targeting review PMID 42442624. reflection.text:
I concluded microtubule destabilizers from the mid-dose 1 uM large-nucleus/multinucleation signal (frac_large_nucleus z=+61.1) and 5/10 destabilizer atlas match, discounting the high-dose 10 uM stabilizer match as an n=6 toxicity artifact. Truth on unblinding was mitoxantrone, a DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor and DNA inhibitor, scored as DNA replication, so the MoA call was wrong and the initial 0.68 confidence was over-calibrated as the review stated.

I was misled by antimitotic-mimic morphology: cell rounding z=+39.4, eccentricity loss, tubulin texture change and reduced density look tubulin-like but are secondary to topo II-induced G2/M arrest and cytokinesis failure. The atlas comparison amplified this because I over-weighted the 5/10 destabilizer vote while dismissing the near-tie protein synthesis 4/10 vote and later combined protein synthesis 5/10 signal, and I never carried a DNA replication hypothesis. My acquisition choice caused the failure to correct: spending the 2-well budget on 10 uM and 1 uM left no well for the requested 0.3 uM test, so dose_response for tub_mean and multinucleation failed for needing 3 wells.

The lesson is to discard extreme z-scores from n=6 wells, require replication for single-well n=46 nuclear phenotypes, and retain DNA-damage/cytokinesis-failure hypotheses when large nuclei, low solidity and multinucleation occur without direct evidence of tubulin loss versus bundles.

## PI review

Verdict: request experiment.

Do not approve: the high-dose support for stabilizers is unreliable (dose index 7, 10 µM, n=6 cells, cosine similarities 0.43-0.51, and e4 states destabilizers cannot be excluded), while the sole informative mid-dose well (dose index 5, 1 µM, rep 1, 46 cells) is single-replicate, its atlas nearly ties Microtubule destabilizers (5/10, mean 0.754) with Protein synthesis (4/10, mean 0.742), and its multinucleation/large-nucleus phenotype also fits Aurora/cytokinesis failure rather than uniquely destabilizers. Thus 0.68 is over-calibrated. One affordable test should discriminate: acquire dose index 4 (0.3 µM), replicate 1, and run the atlas/phenotype comparison on that less-lethal dose to test for dose-dependent tubulin loss versus stabilizer bundles or non-tubulin toxicity.

Requested: Acquire dose index 4 (0.3 µM), replicate 1, then compare its profile/atlas and tubulin phenotype to the 1 µM well.

## Unblinding

Compound: **mitoxantrone** (PubChem CID [4212](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/4212))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor; DNA inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Microtubule destabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA replication**.

## Reflection

I concluded microtubule destabilizers from the mid-dose 1 uM large-nucleus/multinucleation signal (frac_large_nucleus z=+61.1) and 5/10 destabilizer atlas match, discounting the high-dose 10 uM stabilizer match as an n=6 toxicity artifact. Truth on unblinding was mitoxantrone, a DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor and DNA inhibitor, scored as DNA replication, so the MoA call was wrong and the initial 0.68 confidence was over-calibrated as the review stated.

I was misled by antimitotic-mimic morphology: cell rounding z=+39.4, eccentricity loss, tubulin texture change and reduced density look tubulin-like but are secondary to topo II-induced G2/M arrest and cytokinesis failure. The atlas comparison amplified this because I over-weighted the 5/10 destabilizer vote while dismissing the near-tie protein synthesis 4/10 vote and later combined protein synthesis 5/10 signal, and I never carried a DNA replication hypothesis. My acquisition choice caused the failure to correct: spending the 2-well budget on 10 uM and 1 uM left no well for the requested 0.3 uM test, so dose_response for tub_mean and multinucleation failed for needing 3 wells.

The lesson is to discard extreme z-scores from n=6 wells, require replication for single-well n=46 nuclear phenotypes, and retain DNA-damage/cytokinesis-failure hypotheses when large nuclei, low solidity and multinucleation occur without direct evidence of tubulin loss versus bundles.

What was right:
- Recognized high-dose 10 uM well with only 6 cells and reduced density was largely cytotoxic and unreliable for a stabilizer call with similarities 0.43-0.51.
- Captured severe nuclear perturbation at 1 uM with 46 cells with large-nucleus and multinucleation features and reduced density.
- Lowered confidence from 0.68 to 0.38 after critique because mid-dose atlas nearly tied destabilizers 5/10 mean 0.754 with protein synthesis 4/10 mean 0.742 and phenotype also fit Aurora/cytokinesis failure.

What was wrong or missed:
- Over-weighted 5/10 destabilizer atlas hit at 1 uM while ignoring the protein synthesis tie and combined 5/10 protein synthesis signal and never testing DNA replication.
- Treated cell rounding, tubulin contrast and microscopist microtubule/actin suggestions as tubulin-specific despite n=6 extreme z-scores and e4 stating destabilizers could not be excluded.
- Exhausted the 2-well budget on 10 uM plus 1 uM with no replicates, making tubulin-loss versus bundle dose trend untestable and the requested 0.3 uM discriminating well impossible.

Proposed next experiment: Titrate 0.1-1 uM mitoxantrone with gammaH2AX, phospho-H3 and DNA content plus alpha-tubulin washout/regrowth versus vincristine and etoposide controls to test primary tubulin loss versus secondary mitotic failure from topoisomerase II inhibition.
